reviews.title: Nguyễn Ngọc Thuỳ Dương · IELTS 48 · W09 · Đề 1
reviews.scopeMarkdown: **Số từ bài gốc: 214 từ**, đếm trên nguyên văn bằng cách tách theo khoảng trắng; đủ tối thiểu 150 từ nhưng vượt 14 từ so với giới hạn 150–200 từ của lớp. Cô chỉ chấm Đề 1 đã gõ; không chấm Đề 2 hoặc bản scan.
reviews.overall: Cô yêu cầu em sửa và nộp lại. Bài này em làm còn ẩu ở những lỗi câu cụ thể: “These numbers, however, still below…” thiếu động từ chính, còn “Italy… grew” đặt tên nước làm chủ thể tăng. Số liệu Belgium cũng chưa đúng, khiến bài mất quan hệ đồng hạng cuối kỳ. Em đã vận dụng cấu trúc with và after which, nhưng cần dùng kiến thức ấy trong câu hoàn chỉnh, đúng dữ liệu. Overview còn thiếu thông tin thấp nhất và bài vượt giới hạn độ dài. Mục đích đi học là ghi chép, hiểu và vận dụng để tự viết; em đọc lại bài học và tự sửa các câu được đánh dấu.
reviews.dataGrouping: Em đặt Germany, Italy và France trong Detail 1; United Kingdom và Belgium trong Detail 2. Cách chia này hợp lý theo thứ hạng cuối kỳ, nên Cô giữ cả nhóm và thứ tự trình bày. France có đỉnh và đứng đầu năm 2004; em đã chọn được mốc này, cần giữ khi rút bài. Hai nước ở Detail 2 cùng đạt khoảng 28% năm 2012, thấp hơn ba nước đã nêu ở Detail 1.

reviews.originalEssay:
The given line graph illustrates the share of female representatives in parliaments in five European nations between 2000 and 2012.
   Overall, there was an increase in the proportion of women holding parliamentary seats in all the surveyed, with the UK witnessing the most pronounced rise. Notably, in the last year given, Italy recorded the highest figure.
   To elaborate, in 2000, the percentage of women represented in parliament in Germany stood at approximately 33%, the highest figure on the chart, before remaining relatively stable and rising to just over 35% in 2012. Italy, meanwhile, grew more sharply, from 26% in 2000 to nearly 40% in 2012.  The figure for France, conversely, rose dramatically, going from 25% to 37% in 2004 and before dropping markedly by about 10% in 2008 and then gradually increasing to 32% in the final year.
   Regarding the remaining, both the UK and Belgium experienced considerable growth. Starting at the lowest point of 5% in 2000, the figure for the UK increased significantly to approximately 20% in 2008 before reaching nearly 30% in the final year. Belgium; likewise, saw a notable rise from around 12% to 25% over the first four years, after which the figure remained virtually unchanged until 2012. These numbers, however, still below those of Germany, Italy, and France.

To elaborate, in 2000, the percentage of women represented in parliament in Germany stood at approximately 33%, the highest figure on the chart, before remaining relatively stable and rising to just over 35% in 2012. Italy, meanwhile, grew more sharply, from 26% in 2000 to nearly 40% in 2012.  The figure for France, conversely, rose dramatically, going from 25% to 37% in 2004 and before dropping markedly by about 10% in 2008 and then gradually increasing to 32% in the final year.

Regarding the remaining, both the UK and Belgium experienced considerable growth. Starting at the lowest point of 5% in 2000, the figure for the UK increased significantly to approximately 20% in 2008 before reaching nearly 30% in the final year. Belgium; likewise, saw a notable rise from around 12% to 25% over the first four years, after which the figure remained virtually unchanged until 2012. These numbers, however, still below those of Germany, Italy, and France.

The given pie charts illustrate the main reasons why students chose a particular university in the UK between 1997 and 2007.
   Overall, the proportion of students choosing a university for its suitable degree courses was the highest in both years, while the figure for proximity to the parental home increased the most. The figure for proximity to the parental home, meanwhile, increased more sharply, more than doubling from 10% to 22% over the ten-year period. Similarly, the percentage of students choosing a university because of the quality of teaching rose moderately from 15% to 18%.

The given bar chart illustrates the annual pay, in thousands of US dollars, for doctors and other workers in seven countries in 2004.

Overall, doctors earned considerably more than other workers in all seven countries. The US recorded the highest figure for doctors, while Finland had the lowest. Also of note is that Switzerland and France had the same level of pay for doctors, whereas the figure for other workers was highest in the US.

To elaborate, doctors in the US earned an impressive 120 thousand US dollars, marking the highest point in the chart. This was followed by Switzerland and France, with both figures standing at around 70 thousand dollars. The respective figures for doctors in the Czech Republic and Germany were approximately 64 and 63 thousand dollars, while Italy recorded around 60 thousand dollars. Finland had the lowest figure, at only 50 thousand dollars.

Regarding other workers, the US also recorded the highest figure, at around 46 thousand dollars, followed by Switzerland at 40 thousand. France had a figure of approximately 29 thousand dollars, while Finland recorded around 26 thousand. The figures for Italy, the Czech Republic and Germany were the same, at about 20 thousand dollars each. These numbers, however, were considerably lower than those for doctors in every country.

Tuy nhiên, Overview nói Economics đứng đầu mục tutors, trong khi Commerce đạt 93% và Economics chỉ 90%; hai ngành cùng đạt 95% ở mục teaching. Mở bài còn gần nguyên câu chữ đề. Khi chuyển sang Law, em cần gọi tên ngành ngay và giữ đúng nghĩa “very good” thay vì nói chung là hài lòng. Cô yêu cầu em sửa các điểm này và nộp lại.
reviews.dataGrouping: Detail 1 trình bày Commerce rồi Economics; Detail 2 dành cho Law. Cách chia theo khóa học này hợp lý với bảng và làm nổi bật mức cao của Commerce cùng sự đối lập giữa các mục ở Economics. Tuy nhiên, câu đầu Detail 2 phải nêu rõ Law, vì đoạn ngay trước vừa nói về Economics; liên kết “Regarding the remaining” chưa xác định rõ nhóm được đo.

reviews.originalEssay:
The given table illustrates the percentages of first-year students who gave a “very good” rating to the resources provided by a college for three courses.

Overall, Commerce received the most positive ratings in most categories, while Economics recorded the highest figures for teaching and tutors. Also of note is that Law had the lowest percentage for teaching, whereas Economics received the least positive ratings for pre-course information and other resources.

To elaborate, an impressive 95% of Commerce students gave a “very good” rating to pre-course information and teaching, marking the highest figures for this course. The percentages for tutors, printed resources and other resources were also relatively high, at 93%, 85% and 81% respectively. A different pattern was true for Economics, where teaching received the highest rating, at 95%, followed by tutors at 90%. However, only 59% and 60% of students gave positive ratings to pre-course information and other resources respectively.

Regarding the remaining, 80% of students were satisfied with other resources, making this the highest figure for the course. This was followed by tutors, at 76%, while pre-course information and printed resources recorded similar figures of 72% and 70%. Teaching, however, was rated the lowest, at just 62%, considerably below the corresponding figures for the other two courses.

The given table illustrates the numbers of universities ranked among the world’s top 200 in Biology, Medicine and Psychology in five countries in 2011.

Overall, the USA recorded the highest figures in all three subjects, while New Zealand had the lowest numbers. Also of note is that Biology was the most represented subject in the USA and the UK, whereas Psychology had the highest figures in Australia and Canada.

To elaborate, an impressive 69 universities in the USA were ranked in the world’s top 200 for Biology, marking the highest figure in the table. The respective numbers for Medicine and Psychology were also high, at 54 and 58. A similar pattern was seen in the UK, where Biology recorded the highest figure, at 30 universities, followed by Psychology at 29 and Medicine at 24. However, the figures for the UK were considerably lower than those for the USA in all three subjects.

Regarding the remaining countries, Australia and Canada recorded the same number of universities for Biology, at 9 each. However, Australia had slightly higher figures for Medicine and Psychology, at 13 and 17 respectively, compared with 12 and 14 in Canada. Psychology was the most represented subject in both countries. New Zealand, by contrast, had the lowest figures in all three subjects, with 6 universities in Biology, only 2 in Medicine and 4 in Psychology.
